slides.title: Before you say kāfir, read 17:15
slides.promise: The Arabic root behind one carelessly used word.

slides.head: Handled with care, or thrown?
slides.body: A word can be handled with care or thrown without thought. Kufr is one of the most thrown-about words in religious speech.

slides.head: The root means to cover
slides.body: K-f-r carries the sense of covering what is already there. A farmer could be called kāfir: he covers a seed with soil (Surah al-Hadid, 57:20).

slides.head: Only what is present can be covered
slides.body: In Surah al-Baqarah (2:89) the truth came to a people, they recognised it, and then rejected it. Rejection came after recognition.

slides.head: Two things we blur
slides.body: "Non-Muslim" is an outward identity anyone can see. Kāfir asks what no one can see: what reached them, and whether they knowingly turned away.

slides.head: Whose picture of Islam?
slides.body: Someone may be turning away from a distorted picture of Islam. That picture may have been painted partly by Muslims themselves.

slides.head: Surah al-Isra, 17:15
slides.body: "We would never punish until We had sent a messenger." We who see only the surface have little ground for quick verdicts.

slides.quote: Truth does not need cruelty to protect it.
